data.name: Izma
data.gender_notes: Izma is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'azama', which means 'to be heavy, to become strong'. In Islamic history, Izma is the name of the mother of Prophet Solomon (AS). She was known for her strength and courage in protecting her son from adversaries. The name Izma carries the meaning “Mother of a lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Izma usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of a lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of maternal strength and protection in Islam.
data.etymology: Izma belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of a lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Izma total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.
